label: Bark
text: Smooth and greenish on young trees, with lighter patches. With age it turns reddish brown to dark gray, cut by dark furrows into long, rounded, finely scaly ridges.

label: Needles
text: Soft, flexible, 3 to 5 inches long, and in bundles of five: count them to tell it from the two-needled Austrian and Scots pines on campus. Fine white lines of pores along each needle give the tree its blue-green cast. Each bundle lasts about two years.

label: Pollen cones
text: In April, clusters of small, cylindrical yellow pollen cones crowd the new shoots. The seed cones that will become next year's long cones start out light green tinged with red.

label: Cones
text: Long, slender, often curved, 4 to 8 inches, hanging on short stalks, with thin scales that carry no prickles and are sticky with resin. They take two summers to ripen and let their seeds go in July and August.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray-brown to bronze on young trees, dotted with horizontal lenticels. It then splits into long, narrow plates whose edges curl away from the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Feathery, 5 to 8 inches long, divided once into 15 to 30 small oval leaflets, or twice, into four to seven pairs of side branches of leaflets. The leaflets are shiny dark green above and yellow-green beneath.

label: Thorns
text: Wild trees grow stiff, branched thorns on the trunk and lower limbs. As a tree ages it stops making them in the upper and outer crown, but they keep coming on the lower trunk and its sprouts. The trees planted on campus are thornless selections.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Pods
text: Flat, reddish-brown pods 12 to 18 inches long that twist into corkscrews and darken almost to black as they ripen. They hang on through the winter and are messy once they fall.

label: Bark
text: Dark or light gray, split by shallow furrows into broad, hard, scaly ridges. Where a branch has torn away or the bark is cut, the inner layer shows reddish to pink.

label: Leaves
text: About 7 inches long, with 7 to 11 lobes cut less than halfway to the midrib, each ending in a few bristle-tipped teeth: shallower gaps than pin oak's. Dull green, with small tufts of hair where the veins meet beneath. Some dead leaves hang on into winter.

label: Catkins
text: In April and May the male flowers hang in yellowish-green catkins 2 to 4 inches long as the leaves open. The female flowers are tiny, about an eighth of an inch, and take two years to become acorns.

label: Acorns
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half long, smooth and brown, alone or in pairs on a very short stalk. The wide, shallow cap covers only the top quarter. A tree may be forty before it bears any.

label: Bark
text: Salmon to rust-colored on young trunks and branches, peeling year round in tough, papery curls that stay on the tree. Old trunks thicken at the base into dark, flat, scaly ridges, while the limbs above keep peeling.

label: Leaves
text: Two to three and a half inches long, pointed, with a wedge-shaped base and doubly toothed edges, almost diamond-shaped. Pale and waxy beneath, with seven to nine pairs of veins. A modest yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: The male catkins form at the twig tips in fall and wait there all winter as stiff little clusters. In April or May they lengthen and shed their pollen; the small female catkins come out with the leaves.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Seed catkins
text: Upright, cone-like seed catkins an inch to an inch and a half long, among the leaves. They break apart on the tree, shedding tiny winged nutlets: about 400,000 make a pound.

label: Bark
text: Greenish gray and smooth on young trees. With age it darkens and splits into low, narrow ridges that interlace in a tight, regular net, quite unlike sugar maple's long, loose plates.

label: Leaves
text: Broad, five- to seven-lobed, 4 to 10 inches long, the lobes ending in a few long, fine points, much like sugar maple's. Turn one over: Norway maple's is glossy green underneath. Its fall color is yellow.

label: Flowers
text: Upright, rounded clusters of bright yellow-green flowers open in spring just before the leaves, lighting the bare crown yellow-green. Few maples flower as heavily.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras with wings 1½ to 2 inches long, spread out almost in a straight line. Sugar maple's pair hang closer, in a horseshoe. They ripen in September and October and seed freely into nearby woods.

label: Bark
text: Smooth on young trees. Old trunks are gray-brown to nearly black, rough with deep vertical furrows broken by horizontal cracks, the scaly ridges starting to peel. The inner bark is yellow-orange.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches long, oblong, edged with 6 to 10 pairs of coarse teeth or shallow lobes rather than the deep, rounded lobes of white oak. Slightly glossy above; white-felted beneath, on a short yellowish stalk.

label: Catkins
text: In April, yellow-green male catkins 2 to 4 inches long hang among the opening leaves. The female flowers are short spikes, green to red. All are pollinated by the wind.

label: Acorns
text: Shiny brown, half to three-quarters of an inch long, often in twos to fours. The cap, with grayish scales and fine hairs, covers a third to half of the nut. Good crops come every three to five years.

label: Bark
text: Purplish gray on old trunks, deeply grooved and broken into thick scales.

label: Needles
text: Rigid, curved like little sabers, up to an inch long and tipped with a sharp spine, spreading all around the twig. Color runs from dull green to blue to silvery white from one tree to the next.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small orange to reddish pollen cones cluster near the tips of the shoots in May, shed their pollen, and fall.

label: Cones
text: Two to four inches long, hanging, green with a violet bloom before they ripen light brown. The thin tips of the scales are wavy and finely toothed, which makes the cone look papery and ragged.

label: Bark
text: Light gray to gray-brown, varying a good deal from tree to tree. Smooth on young trunks; old ones furrow into long, thick, irregular plates.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and as wide, with two small lobes at the base and three larger ones above, each with a few deep notches but no fine teeth. Red maple's leaf, by contrast, is toothed all round. The base is heart-shaped.

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-yellow flowers dangle in tassels up to 3 inches long, each on a thread-thin stalk, as the leaves unfold in spring. Male and female flowers are separate.

label: Fruit
text: Paired, papery-winged samaras about an inch long, joined in a U with the wings nearly parallel. Green over the summer, they ripen brown and spin down in fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and light gray on young trunks. Old trunks thicken and darken to gray, divided by vertical ridges into large, plate-like scales.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, a little broader than long, with three main triangular lobes and often two small ones near the base, coarsely and irregularly toothed all round. Grayish beneath, with hairs along the veins.

label: Flowers
text: Small flowers in short-stalked, drooping clusters, well before the leaves appear. Trees differ: some carry male flowers, some female, some both.

label: Fruit
text: Pairs of samaras about three-quarters of an inch long, joined in a narrow V and hanging on long stalks. Red, pink or yellow, they turn tan and fall by early summer.

label: Bark
text: Grayish to reddish brown with shallow furrows; on mature trees it loosens and peels from trunk and branches. A wild tree usually keeps one dominant trunk, often twisted.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny scales pressed flat to the twig in opposite pairs, each pair overlapping the next, making flat, fan-like sprays. Look closely: each scale carries a small raised gland near its tip. Darker green above, paler beneath.

label: Cones
text: Small, oblong cones a third to half an inch long, yellowish when young and ripening light brown, when their few thin scales spread open.

label: Winter color
text: Through the winter the sprays lose much of their green and turn bronze or yellowish brown, most on plants in wind and full sun. The green comes back in spring.

label: Shape
text: Every limb climbs steeply beside the trunk, so the crown is barely wider than a column. It is the shape that makes the tree, seen from a long way off.

label: Bark
text: Gray-black and deeply furrowed, the old trunk ribbed and flaring into buttresses at its base.

label: Leaves
text: Shiny, triangular to diamond-shaped, 2 to 4½ inches long. On the long new shoots they are wider than long, with a straight or faintly heart-shaped base; on short shoots, tapered to a wedge.

label: Catkins
text: In early spring, before the leaves, the bare twigs hang with red male catkins. Black poplars bear male and female flowers on separate trees; the female catkins are green.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray to almost black, split by deep furrows into flat, vertical ridges.

label: Needles
text: Three to six inches long, two to a bundle, stiff, sharp-tipped and dark bluish green; straight or a little twisted. Each stays on the tree up to four years.

label: Pollen cones
text: Yellow, cylindrical pollen cones half to three-quarters of an inch long crowd the base of each new shoot, or candle, in late April and May. The small purplish seed cones sit at the candle's tip.

label: Cones
text: Hard, oval, brown cones two and a half to three inches long, each scale ending in a short, blunt point. They start out half an inch long and ripen in fall.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and reddish to grayish brown on young trees. With age it darkens and cracks into shallow fissures.

label: Leaves
text: About five inches long, with five bristle-tipped lobes and U-shaped gaps cut nearly to the midrib. The midrib runs out through the tip. Glossy and the same green on both sides, with small tufts of tan hairs where the veins meet beneath.

label: Catkins
text: In spring, drooping yellow-green catkins of male flowers hang among the new leaves. The female flowers sit on short stalks where the leaves join the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Small and nearly round, a quarter to half an inch, light to reddish brown, alone or in twos and threes. The thin, smooth, saucer-like cap covers only a quarter to a third. A tree may be 15 or 20 before it bears.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown and lightly furrowed on young trunks. Old trees turn dark gray, with deep furrows between prominent ridges.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long and wide: far smaller than basswood's. Heart-shaped with a finely toothed edge, semi-glossy above and paler below. In fall they go chartreuse, golden only if the tree is stressed.

label: Flowers
text: In late June and early July, clusters of five to seven creamy-yellow flowers hang from the middle of a long, pale, strap-shaped bract.

label: Fruit
text: Small, round, hairy nutlets, a quarter inch across, hanging in clusters from the same strap-shaped bract, which carries them off on the wind like a wing. Pale green, ripening tan in late summer.

label: Bark
text: Thin and smooth on young trees, purplish, greenish or silvery brown. With age it thickens and breaks into small, flaky scales.

label: Needles
text: Stiff, four-sided, glossy dark green, up to an inch long, each standing on a tiny woody peg. On the upper side of the twig they point forward and overlap; below they spread sideways, like the bristles of a brush.

label: Pollen cones
text: Small pollen cones cluster along last year's shoots. The young seed cones are purple and stand upright; once pollinated by the wind they turn green and tip over to hang down.

label: Cones
text: Four to six inches long and hanging, greenish or violet when young and silvery brown when ripe. The thin scales end in a blunt, irregularly toothed point. The seeds are black with a pale brown wing.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and grayish white on young trunks, with a faint honeycomb pattern. As it ages, small patches flake away to show orange beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Oblong, long-pointed and a little lopsided at the base, with a row of large, sharp teeth. The side veins run straight and parallel, each ending in a tooth. Fall color varies from yellow to burgundy.

label: Flowers
text: Tiny greenish flowers cluster where the leaves meet the new shoots in spring, easily missed.

label: Fruit
text: Small, hard, lopsided fruits, egg- to kidney-shaped with two tiny beaks, along the twig in fall. Each holds one seed.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, rough and furrowed into ridges on old trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Two to three inches long, emerald green, in clusters of three to five on short side shoots. The veins fork again and again in pairs and never join in a net.

label: Pollen cones
text: Ginkgo has no flowers. Trees are male or female: the males bear small pollen cones in spring, the females bare ovules at the ends of stalks. Fertilization is by swimming sperm, as in ferns and cycads.

label: Seeds
text: Not fruit but seeds, plum-like and yellow-orange, only on female trees. A fleshy outer coat surrounds a hard, smooth, cream-colored shell.

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth on the branches. The trunk is furrowed lengthwise into narrow, flat-topped ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Up to ten inches long, coarsely toothed, dark green above and a matte gray below, the base unequal. Young leaves are downy underneath and lose the hairs with age. Littleleaf linden's are a third the size.

label: Flowers
text: Drooping clusters of yellow flowers up to five inches long, each with five petals and a burst of stamens, hang from the middle of a pale, leafy bract.

label: Fruit
text: Hard, dry, downy nutlets the size of a pea, cream to brown, hanging on stalks from the same bract, which stays attached and spins the cluster away on the wind.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and silver-gray when young. With age it breaks into long, thin scales that give old trunks a shaggy look. Under them the inner bark is orange.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches, with five lobes cut deeply toward the center. Medium green on top. Fall color is a mix of yellow, brown and green.

label: Flowers
text: Dense tufts of greenish-yellow to red flowers burst from the bare twigs in early spring, before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Large paired samaras, the wings spreading at nearly a right angle. They ripen in late spring.

label: Bark
text: Thin, tight and bluish gray, stretched smooth over a trunk that ripples in irregular ridges. Beech also has smooth gray bark, but over a round trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long, egg-shaped to oblong, doubly toothed with sharp teeth: big teeth carrying small ones. Dull bluish green above and paler below.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female catkins on the same tree in spring: the male ones 1 to 2½ inches long and hanging; the female ones under an inch.

label: Fruit
text: Small nutlets, a third of an inch long, each at the base of a green, three-lobed, leafy bract an inch or more long, the middle lobe widest. The bracts hang in loose clusters and carry the nutlets off on the wind.

label: Bark
text: Brown to gray, scaly, and on old trunks furrowed so deeply that the ridges stand out like twisted rope, crossing and rejoining up the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to fourteen inches long and divided into as many as 23 oval leaflets, dark blue-green, turning a plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: White pea flowers, very fragrant, hang in loose chains up to eight inches long in late spring, like a white wisteria.

label: Spines
text: Short, sharp spines grow in pairs where each leaf meets the twig, made from the leaf's stipules. They appear in the second half of a shoot's first year. Honeylocust's thorns are long, branched and grow from the trunk.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark
text: Fibrous, dark red-brown to gray, peeling in many thin vertical strips. The base of the trunk flares out into buttresses and flutes.

label: Knees
text: Near water the roots send up knobby, conical knees, sometimes in crowds around the tree. What they are for is uncertain; one idea is that they help bring air to roots in waterlogged mud.

label: Foliage
text: Soft, flat needles a quarter to three-quarters of an inch long, in two flat rows along slender side shoots. Yellow-green in spring, sage green in summer. In fall whole shoots drop with their needles still on.

label: Cones
text: Round and wrinkled, three-quarters of an inch to an inch across, purplish green ripening to brown in October, made of thick, irregular scales.

label: Buds
text: Big, glossy, red-brown winter buds, coated in resin that makes them sticky to the touch.

label: Leaves
text: Five to seven leaflets spread from the end of a long stalk like the fingers of a hand, each 5 to 12 inches long, widest toward the tip and doubly toothed.

label: Flowers
text: Upright spikes up to a foot tall, packed with large creamy-white flowers, each with a blotch in the throat that starts yellow and turns red-speckled.

label: Fruit
text: A leathery, prickly husk 1 to 2 inches across splits open in fall to drop one or two large, shiny brown seeds, each with a pale scar where it was attached.

label: Bark
text: White, peeling in thin papery strips to show orange-brown inner bark. Older trunks pick up black markings.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, oval with a pointed tip, irregularly toothed, dark green, with hairs along the veins underneath. A rich golden yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female catkins on the same tree. The male ones hang up to four inches long from the twig tips; the female ones are smaller, under an inch and a quarter, and stand upright.

label: Seed catkins
text: The female catkins become hanging, cone-like clusters packed with tiny winged seeds, ripening in late summer and falling apart to release them.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown to gray and scaly at the base of the trunk. Higher up it flakes away in patches, light gray over white to cream, a mottled pattern sometimes called camouflage bark.

label: Leaves
text: Broad, like a maple's, 4 to 9 inches wide and usually wider than long, with three to five coarsely toothed lobes, but growing one at a time along the twig, not in pairs. The flared base of each leafstalk hides next year's bud.

label: Flowers
text: In April, tiny flowers in round heads, the males greenish yellow and the females red, each head hanging from its own stalk.

label: Seed balls
text: Fuzzy brown balls half an inch to an inch across, usually one to a stalk 3 to 6 inches long. They hang into winter, then break up, releasing seeds with downy tufts on the wind.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown to almost black, deeply fissured with age, on a short trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, with three to seven pairs of rounded lobes, on a stalk so short the leaf seems to sit on the twig. At the base the blade curls into two small ear lobes. They stay green late, then go yellow and brown.

label: Catkins
text: Slender, yellowish-green male catkins 2 to 3 inches long hang with the new leaves in spring. The tiny female flowers sit on short spikes, three or four together.

label: Acorns
text: Egg-shaped, about an inch long, one to five together at the end of a stalk 1 to 4 inches long. The cup covers a quarter to a third of the nut. They ripen in one season.

label: Bark
text: Gray, cut very deep into narrow, flattened vertical ridges.

label: Leaves
text: Six to twelve inches long, leathery, broadest toward the tip. The two middle gaps cut nearly to the midrib, almost dividing the leaf in two. Wedge-shaped at the base; grayish and finely downy beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female flowers in separate catkins on the same tree, as the leaves emerge in spring. The males hang in long, drooping strings.

label: Acorns
text: Oval, up to an inch and a half across, a quarter to half sunk in a deep cup whose rim is fringed with long, curling scales, like a chestnut's spiny bur. They ripen in one season.

label: Bark
text: Smooth, reddish brown and glossy, marked with horizontal lenticels like a cherry's, and peeling. On old trunks it turns gray and scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Broad, oval, sharp-tipped, 2 to 5½ inches long, in pairs. Dark green above and grayish green beneath, hanging a little. They drop in fall without much color.

label: Flowers
text: Upright plumes 6 to 12 inches long, packed with small creamy-white flowers, open in June for about two weeks.

label: Seed capsules
text: Clusters of dry, warty, oblong capsules about three-quarters of an inch long, green turning yellow, which hang on through the winter.

label: Bark and thorns
text: Thin and gray, breaking into narrow scales that flake off to show orange-red beneath. Stems and branches carry slender, very sharp thorns, sometimes even on the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, triangular, with three to five sharply toothed lobes and a squared-off base on an inch-long stalk. Glossy dark green above, lighter beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters of up to fifty half-inch white flowers with pink anthers, between April and June. They last about ten days, and the smell is unpleasant: they are pollinated by midges.

label: Fruit
text: Glossy, bright red, a quarter inch across, in heavy clusters from September. They hang through the winter, the season's color after the leaves drop.
